description.narrative: HALO Trust’s programme in Ukraine aims to reduce the risks posed by landmines and other explosive ordnance so that civilians can return home safely, regain access to land and essential services, and rebuild their livelihoods. Through the HARPS project, HALO and its partners will deliver an integrated package of humanitarian mine action across eight oblasts: Chernihiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Kherson, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Sumy, and Zaporizhzhia. The programme combines non-technical survey, clearance, explosive ordnance disposal, and explosive ordnance risk education with survivor support and national capacity strengthening. Over four years, HALO and its partners aim to release 4,943,200 square metres of land through clearance, reduction, and cancellation; deliver risk education to 116,800 people; and provide psychosocial support to 2,484 survivors. The programme prioritises conflict-affected rural communities, including internally displaced people, women, children, older persons, and people with disabilities, who face heightened protection risks and barriers to safe return. A strong focus of the programme is localisation and sustainability. HALO works closely with Peaceful Heaven of Kharkiv (PHK) to strengthen Ukrainian mine action capacity and support a gradual transition towards nationally led implementation. In partnership with Mercy Corps, the programme also links mine action to agricultural recovery, food security, and livelihoods, helping communities make productive use of land once it is safe. Across all activities, HALO applies gender-sensitive, inclusive, and environmentally responsible approaches to ensure that assistance is effective, equitable, and aligned with Ukraine’s National Mine Action Strategy. The programme is grounded in a gender and intersectional analysis of explosive ordnance contamination in Ukraine
